reading.identification: Mid-to-late 19th-century plastered-brick corner commercial house at Korenmarkt/Hooiaard, Ghent: four storeys of dwelling/office over a tall bluestone-pier ground floor now trading as a café, under a red-pantile hipped roof.
reading.notes:
Storey count is reconstructed, not sighted: set B is cut off above the second floor (dashed outline) and set A's facade has a mesh seam that duplicates one window band. Ground+3 is the only reading that closes with the measured 17.4 m ridge — 4.3 + 3x3.3 = 14.2 m eaves, leaving a 3.2 m rise over the 6.7 m depth (~44 deg hip, normal for a Ghent pantile roof). Five storeys would force ~23 deg, which set A contradicts. Heights therefore inferred.

Window metrics: subdivision (two lights plus transom), shallow reveal behind the render face, and the tall ~1:1.9 proportion are directly seen in B at good resolution; the values in metres are scaled off the assumed storey height, so treat the proportion as measured and the absolute size as +/- 15%.

Ledges: sills seen in B under every upper window (stone, projection is marginal at ~8-10 cm — model as explicit geometry but do not exaggerate). String course = the projecting ledge running the length of the facade at shopfront head height, seen in B with the service conduit riding on it; this is the strongest horizontal wedge on the wall and matters for street-level field. Cornice is from set A only (white projecting eaves band under the pantiles) — set A is weak wall evidence but this is a roofline feature it can resolve. No balconies anywhere on either frontage.

Material: render hides the substrate, so brick is the period/place prior, not an observation. What is seen is smooth painted stucco, patched and hairline-cracked, with visible panel joints in the bluestone plinth — hence 0.8 mm RMS. Keep the 1-10 cm regime (patching, joints, plinth panel lines) as a scattering coefficient; meshing it would produce specular garbage at 1.07 cm wavelength. Trim is Belgian bluestone (arduin) at the piers, plinth, corner quoin pier and sills; 'marble' is the nearest dielectric in the available set, denser than the wall.

Corner condition: two street frontages, so the shopfront and the dark plinth return around the Hooiaard corner on a full-height bluestone quoin pier. Give that corner extra silhouette budget — it is the edge most cameras and most rays will see.

Clutter: fronting street is pedestrian with car_access=none. No parked or moving vehicles on this frontage under any circumstances. What set B actually shows and what should be placed instead: café terrace with a large parasol, timber planter troughs on the shopfront shelf, two A-boards on the paving, bicycles leaning at the kerb, a tarped stack, plus wall-mounted CCTV domes, security floodlights, an H100 hydrant plate and the HOOIAARD enamel street plate on the corner pier. The floodlights and cameras are ~20-30 cm bodies on brackets standing off the wall — above the 10 cm threshold and directly in the ground-floor beam path, so they are worth explicit geometry.
